messages:
Priya (Customer): Hey team — our app started getting a bunch of 429s around 11:10 PDT. We're on a Dedicated reserved pool (pool_id: rp-9c4f) and have a burst window configured. This is during a marketing blast, traffic spiked but our SLA says we should have sustained throughput. Any idea what's going on?

Mia (Support): sorry to hear that — can you paste the first 3 failing request ids and a small repro? Also which model & config are you using?

Priya (Customer): sure: req-183a, req-183b, req-183c. model: rw-large-v1, concurrency: 120, preferred_region: us-west-2. We have reserved capacity commit for 6000 tpm and a burst allowance of 2x for up to 5 minutes. The errors look like immediate 429s with header X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0.

Mia (Support): got it. sharing with SRE and Runtime. Can you attach a small curl that reproduces the 429? (no creds in channel)

Priya (Customer): here's a sanitized curl we used locally (token redacted):

```bash
curl -s -X POST
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
  -d '{"model":"rw-large-v1","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":256}'
```

We ramped many parallel requests from their client SDK; ramp started 11:09:55 and 429s at 11:10:07.

Oliver (SRE): I'm looking at the ingress metrics for rp-9c4f. I see the pool hit the configured sustained cap (~100 rps equivalent) at 11:10:05 but the burst token allowance looks depleted by 11:10:08. There's also a pattern of many short-lived connections — the token-bucket refill is per-second and our smoothing kicks in.

Mia (Support): can you clarify "smoothing"? Customer believes 2x burst for 5min should cover this.

Oliver (SRE): short version: the platform enforces two layers — (1) per-tenant sustained throughput (your reserved commit), and (2) burst tokens that allow temporary oversubscription. But burst tokens are distributed across sub-shards and refilled on a cadence. If you send thousands of tiny concurrent requests, you can exhaust per-shard burst pools faster than the global window suggests. That results in 429 responses even if the aggregate burst budget wasn't fully used.

Amos (Runtime): adding detail: we also have a per-connection concurrency limiter (to protect KV/kv-cache and kernel warmup). Rapid fan-out can trigger additional internal rate limits (not surfaced as separate headers today) which shows up as 429 at the API layer.

Priya (Customer): ah — so our client fan-out is the problem, not the committed tokens? But how does that align with SLA (we purchased Dedicated)?

Mia (Support): good question — SLA is for the reserved commit (throughput and uptime), but burst behavior is best-effort within policy. When per-shard limits or concurrency guards trigger, it can look like a quota violation. We should provide immediate mitigation and then recommend config changes.

Oliver (SRE): immediate mitigations: 1) apply a temporary rate-smoothing override on rp-9c4f to increase per-shard burst window for next 30m, 2) add a short token refill (experimental) so small concurrent bursts get spread, 3) if you can throttle client-side concurrency to <100 active requests during the blast, that will prevent the per-conn limiter from firing.

Mia (Support): Priya — do you want us to apply the temporary override while we investigate?

Priya (Customer): yes please. We need to recover traffic within 10 minutes or the campaign will miss conversions.

Mia (Support): on it. escalating to Runtime for the override.

deploy-bot: deploy started by Mia (Support) — change-set: smoothing-override-rp-9c4f 

Amos (Runtime): I applied the smoothing override and bumped per-shard burst TTL to 5m for rp-9c4f. Keep an eye on 429s and let us know if you see progress.

Priya (Customer): seeing 429 rate drop immediately. thanks! Can you explain the root cause so we can prevent this next time?

Amos (Runtime): root cause summary: high fan-out of very short requests caused uneven consumption of distributed burst tokens and hit a per-connection concurrency guard. The reserved commit was not fully saturated globally, but local shard and connection limits were exceeded.

Amos (Runtime): repro steps we used to validate in staging:
1) Start 500 parallel workers each firing 5 rps short requests to rw-large-v1.
2) Observe X-RateLimit-Remaining drop to 0 on a subset of shard responses.
3) Interleave a few long-running streams to exercise KV cache hot-shard eviction.

Example stress script (sanitized):
```python
import requests, threading

def hit():
    for i in range(20):
        r = requests.post('https://staging-api.redwood/generate', json={'model':'rw-large-v1','input':'p'}, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer REDACTED'})
        if r.status_code != 200:
            print('err', r.status_code, r.headers.get('X-RateLimit-Remaining'))

threads = [threading.Thread(target=hit) for _ in range(500)]
for t in threads: t.start()
for t in threads: t.join()
```

Oliver (SRE): follow-up items: 1) make per-shard burst accounting more visible in headers (we'll add X-Shard-Burst-Remaining), 2) update docs about concurrency/fanout guidance for Dedicated pools, 3) expose an SDK helper for client-side smoothing. I'll file a ticket.

Mia (Support): created internal ticket INF-9876 to track root cause and docs updates. Assigning to Amos + Oliver.

Priya (Customer): for now, what's the recommended client change? We use the official SDK which has parallel job queues.

Amos (Runtime): tune client concurrency to a steady rate (e.g., 80 concurrent workers), use exponential backoff on 429 with jitter, and add a small client-side leaky bucket (e.g., allow short bursts but cap instantaneous concurrency). We'll provide a sample config.

Mia (Support): sending sample config now:

```json
{"client_smoothing": {"max_concurrency": 80, "burst_capacity": 200, "backoff": {"base_ms": 100, "cap_ms": 5000}}}
```

Priya (Customer): thanks. can you confirm this incident won't affect billing/credits? We saw a sudden spike in token usage before the 429s.

Oliver (SRE): meter confirms tokens were counted for accepted requests only. Retries that receive immediate 429s are not billed. We'll audit the window and share a billing note. If any overage occurred due to unexpected acceptance, we'll coordinate credits.

Mia (Support): billing note: opened invoice review with Finance (FIN-4012). Will follow up in this thread when resolved.

Amos (Runtime): long-term fixes we propose: fine-grained shard burst smoothing, per-tenant burst capacity visibility, and SDK client smoothing primitives. We'll propose rollout plan in INF-9876.

Priya (Customer): appreciate the quick action. if you can add a recommended SDK config and a short KB about reserved pool fanout gotchas, that would be ideal.

Mia (Support): noted — we'll attach the KB draft here once Oliver and Amos finish. Closing temporary override in 30m unless you request extension.

Priya (Customer): no need to extend, traffic tapering now. thanks everyone :bow:
